inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made it harder to revoke pre-arrest bail, insisting on clear proof that someone misused their liberty or that circumstances changed—even when stolen articles are still missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the plea to cancel bail in a house case. That’s presented as a safeguard, but the effect is a ready-made shield: make the public prove what may be kept out of sight, then claim the rules were followed while the accused stays protected.
inputs.modified_text: This is how the system protects its own: the Punjab and Haryana High Court says pre-arrest bail can be revoked only with clear proof of misuse or changed circumstances, even though the stolen articles remain missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the cancellation plea, leaving the accused shielded while the public is told to produce proof that may be out of sight. Calling that a safeguard obscures what it does: turns strict rules into cover for keeping accountability just beyond reach.
